rounds.text: Creative Newtech Ltd demonstrates exceptional growth and profitability that significantly outpace sector benchmarks, highlighting its underlying fundamental strength [E6, E7, E8, E9, E10]. Compounded sales growth has reached 39% over 5 years and accelerated to 49% over the trailing twelve months, while 5-year compounded profit growth sits at an impressive 49% [E14, E16, E17]. Furthermore, long-term return metrics remain robust, evidenced by a 5-year median return on equity of 22% and a current ROCE of 18.8% [E12, E23]. Valuation support is evident through a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs 2001 per share, which offers a substantial 42.6% margin of safety against the current market price of Rs 1149 [E42, E43]. The rules-based screen reinforces this potential with a high-confidence BUY score of 96 out of 100, supported by positive institutional money flows and a relative-strength rating of 100 [E41, E48, E60]. Conceded: operating cash flow turned negative to Rs -273 Cr in Mar 2026 alongside an increase in debtor days [E31, E58].

Creative Newtech Ltd carries significant fundamental risks that undermine its headline growth figures, most notably a severe cash flow disconnect where operating cash flow plunged to Rs -273 Cr and free cash flow dropped to Rs -276 Cr in March 2026, resulting in a negative cash conversion of -3.90x against reported profit [E30, E31, E32]. This severe cash burn has forced a dramatic surge in borrowings, which spiked to Rs 324 Cr in March 2026 from just Rs 72 Cr a year earlier [E36]. Working capital pressures are intensifying as debtor days stretch from 52.0 to 76.3 days [E58]. Valuation multiples also reflect a rich entry point, with the P/E of 24.59x, P/B of 4.98x, and EV/EBITDA of 18.71x all trading at substantial premiums to their respective sector benchmarks of 19.63x, 1.52x, and 12.08x [E6, E7, E11]. Furthermore, insider commitment shows erosion, with promoter holding decreasing by 6.86% over the last three years [E59] and offering a negligible dividend yield of just 0.04% [E4]. Investors face considerable downside volatility, evidenced by a historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -51.3% and an annualized volatility of 52.7% [E50, E51]. Conceded: the company has demonstrated strong 5-year compounded profit growth of 49.1% alongside a positive 5-year sales growth rate of 39% [E14, E57].

Conceded: operating cash flow dropped to Rs -273 Cr and free cash flow dropped to Rs -276 Cr in March 2026 [E31, E32], and borrowings rose to Rs 324 Cr from Rs 72 Cr [E36]. However, this cash drain occurs alongside comfortable short-term liquidity with a current ratio of 2.36x [E35], while the rules-based screen scores the business 96 out of 100 with a high confidence BUY [E60]. Conceded: debtor days have increased to 76.3 days [E58], but this working capital expansion fuels phenomenal top-line momentum, evidenced by a 49% compounded sales growth rate over the trailing twelve months and 21% YoY sales growth [E16, E61]. Conceded: valuation multiples sit at a premium to sector benchmarks [E6, E7, E11], yet this is entirely justified by elite profitability where ROA of 7.86%, ROCE of 14.89% to 18.8%, and ROE of 19.33% to 21.4% vastly outperform sector medians of 1.94%, 6.33%, and 4.7% respectively [E8, E9, E10, E12, E13]. Conceded: promoter holding decreased over three years [E59], but institutional money flow reads positive with foreign and domestic institutions increasing their stakes [E39, E40, E41], and a DCF model reveals intrinsic value providing a substantial 42.6% margin of safety [E42, E43]. Conceded: historical volatility and drawdowns are elevated [E50, E51], but the price remains supported above its 50-day and 200-day moving averages alongside a perfect relative-strength rating of 100 [E47, E48].

Conceded: the rules-based screen gives a score of 96 out of 100 [E60]. However, relying on this model score ignores the severe reality that operating cash flow for March 2026 collapsed to negative Rs -273 Cr and free cash flow dropped to negative Rs -276 Cr, with cash conversion deteriorating to -3.90x [E30, E31, E32]. Conceded: trailing twelve-month sales growth reached 49% [E16], but this top-line expansion has been achieved by stretching debtor days from 52.0 to 76.3 days [E58], directly causing the negative cash flows and a massive spike in borrowings to Rs 324 Cr from Rs 72 Cr [E36]. Conceded: profitability metrics exceed sector benchmarks [E8, E9, E10], but valuation multiples like the P/E of 24.59x and EV/EBITDA of 18.71x sit at steep premiums to their respective sector benchmarks of 19.63x and 12.08x [E6, E11]. Conceded: institutional stakes increased [E39, E40], but total promoter holding has fallen by 6.86% over the last three years [E59]. Conceded: the technical setup shows the price above its moving averages with a relative-strength rating of 100 [E47, E48], yet this momentum carries an annualised volatility of 52.7% and a historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -51.3% [E50, E51], exposing investors to extreme downside risks that a DCF margin of safety [E43] cannot cushion.

While the bear highlights negative cash flow [E30, E31, E32] and increased borrowings [E36], these are the results of aggressive expansion where trailing twelve-month sales growth of 49% [E16] and profit growth of 36% [E19] vastly exceed sector medians of 11.8% [E69] and 17.1% [E68]. Conceded: debtor days have increased [E58], yet the company maintains a comfortable current ratio of 2.36x [E35] and a moderate debt-to-equity ratio of 0.89x [E34], indicating that the capital used to fuel this expansion is being managed within safe limits. Conceded: promoter holdings have declined [E59], but this is offset by positive institutional money flow [E41] and increasing stakes from both foreign and domestic institutions [E39, E40]. Despite historical volatility [E51] and drawdowns [E50], the current momentum is fundamentals-led because five-year profit growth of 49% has outpaced price growth of 37% [E53], resulting in a relative-strength rating of 100 [E48] and a substantial 42.6% margin of safety against the intrinsic value of Rs 2001 [E42, E43]. Finally, the current price only implies 10.4% earnings growth [E44], which is highly conservative given the company's five-year compounded profit growth of 49% [E17] and its rules-based buy score of 96 out of 100 [E60].

Conceded: five-year profit growth of 49% outpaced price growth of 37% [E53]. However, the bull's framing of aggressive expansion as a justification for negative cash flows ignores the staggering scale of the deterioration, with operating cash flow collapsing to negative ₹273 Cr and free cash flow plunging to negative ₹276 Cr in March 2026 [E31, E32, E33]. This capital drain directly forced borrowings to surge more than fourfold from ₹72 Cr to ₹324 Cr in a single year [E36], rendering the moderate debt-to-equity label [E34] obsolete in the face of acute liquidity consumption. Furthermore, while the bull dismisses insider selling, promoter holdings have contracted significantly by 6.86% over the last three years [E59]. Finally, the claim of safe valuation contrasts sharply with premium multiples that price the stock at 24.59x P/E and 4.98x P/B against sector benchmarks of 19.63x and 1.52x respectively [E6, E7].
